proof_attempt_summary: The run derived and adjudicated a deterministic RankPeel procedure with quadratic oracle-query order, canonical neutrality, replay certificates, and a restricted separator proof. A legal thin-support SEM then showed that the all-C¹-version conditional-mean Jacobian rank is not an observed-law functional under the promised unchanged Conditions 1–3. Positive-density/open-support and execution-local jet/fibre assumptions recover a sound strict-subclass theorem, but that substituted kernel was graded incremental and could not meet the field floor.
tldr: Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang already identify the full binary adjacency matrix of a nonlinear latent hierarchy and already reuse measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates.  RankPeel is a deterministic population protocol with at most \(p^2+p\) combined observed-law queries, worst-case \(\Theta(p^2)\) query order, and \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping.  This note corrects and qualifies a version-free reading of the anchor's Conditions 1--3: the smooth boundary member \(X_1=\cdots=X_4=H\) admits conditional-mean versions with different transverse Jacobian ranks, so the unchanged conditions do not by themselves define the present law-level rank oracle.  Exact recovery has two proved strict-subclass routes.  The sharp abstract route assumes query-local first-jet determinacy and latent-separator-relative pointwise fibre coherence.  The new support-regular route assumes that every queried predictor law is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on an open full-measure set; positive density then fixes first jets, and directed Markovness plus the anchor's almost-sure conditional-sufficiency factorization yields the separator bound without pointwise fibre coherence.  Canonical neutrality, quadratic complexity, and oracle-relative replay retain their stated scope.
gap: The closest nonlinear result already identifies the complete binary adjacency matrix and already uses measured pure descendants as recursive surrogates, but its construction exhaustively searches subset families and gives no explicit polynomial bound on observed rank queries. Its pointwise conditional-mean derivative notation also does not establish invariance across regular-conditional versions.
fill: RankPeel supplies the deterministic pairwise and deletion protocol, a \(p^2+p\) complete-run query bound, and a replay corollary. A law-invariant stability domain prevents arbitrary pointwise versions from entering the oracle, while the exact Conditions 1--3 completeness obligation remains an open theorem-level boundary rather than a new assumption.
